title: Bosch Digital Design System - First General Research
intent: Low-context but thorough summary of the main findings from the first broad internal research on the Bosch Digital Design System (BDDS).
recommended_audiences: product teams needing Bosch-compliant digital outputs

covered_topics: relationship between BDDS, Bosch Brand Guide, FROK, DOCK, Frontify, and Figma
design tokens and Digital Color System 2
excluded_topics: Native-app implementation specifics beyond high-level guidance
Confidential project-specific design adaptations outside core BDDS guidance
scope.research_style: General foundational synthesis rather than full component inventory

executive_summary.short_definition: BDDS is the official Bosch digital extension of the Bosch Brand Guide. It standardizes the design, development, and operation of digital Bosch touchpoints so teams can produce consistent, accessible, high-quality, and brand-compliant interfaces.
executive_summary.main_conclusion: The strongest single-source authority is the Bosch Brand Guide / BDDS documentation, but BDDS should be understood as an ecosystem: Brand Guide + BDDS documentation + Bosch UI Kit in Figma + FROK for implementation + token documentation + accessibility guidance + update/migration communications.
practical_reading: If a team wants Bosch-compliant digital outputs, BDDS is not optional baseline guidance but the default standard for Bosch digital touchpoints.
The system is increasingly token-driven and moving toward a more headless, reusable architecture, which makes it especially relevant for AI-assisted design and code generation.
Accessibility is not a side guideline. It is embedded into the color system, typography, component logic, and legal/compliance framing.

authoritative_sources.source_name: Bosch Digital Design System (BDDS) - Docupedia overview
authoritative_sources.why_it_is_authoritative: Provides the official definition of BDDS, its relation to the Bosch Brand Guide, its objectives, its mandatory character for Bosch products, its key benefits, and named contact roles.
key_takeaways: BDDS is the official extension of the Bosch Brand Guide for digital touchpoints.
BDDS is intended to create high-quality, consistent, accessible, and brand-compliant digital products.
Consistent usage is tied to brand recognition and trust.
BDDS recommends component reuse without modification, close design-development collaboration, and continuous update cycles.

authoritative_sources.source_name: Supporting digital accessibility with the Bosch Digital Design System
authoritative_sources.why_it_is_authoritative: Provides the strongest textual framing of how accessibility, law, typography, color systems, machine readability, and interaction rules are operationalized through BDDS.
key_takeaways: Accessibility is positioned as part of Bosch's brand and digital design responsibility.
Typography, color, layout, alt text, focus logic, captions, and ARIA concerns are all treated as systemized design requirements.
The Bosch Brand Guide is identified as the documentation platform to find the standards.
The presentation explicitly connects BDDS components and color systems to scalable accessibility implementation.

bdds_definition.statement: BDDS is the shared design system for Bosch digital products. It combines design, development, and operational standards into one system so Bosch touchpoints use the same visual language, tools, and reusable resources.
implications: The system is not only a design reference but also a cross-functional alignment mechanism.
It links visual design, frontend implementation, legal compliance, and operational reuse.
It is meant to reduce fragmentation across Bosch digital touchpoints.

relationship_to_brand_guide.statement: BDDS is a digital extension and supplement to the Bosch Brand Guide, not a separate parallel style language.
implications: Brand Guide principles remain upstream authority.
BDDS translates Bosch brand principles into digital-specific assets, rules, patterns, and implementations.
When AI or human designers need the canonical source, Brand Guide + BDDS should be treated as the root documentation layer.

mandatory_nature.statement: BDDS is framed as binding for Bosch products, with central directive support and explicit emphasis on consistent usage for brand trust.
implications: Bosch digital outputs should default to BDDS unless there is a justified exception such as third-party or non-Bosch brand scenarios.
Custom design divergence should be treated as an exception, not the norm.
AI systems used at Bosch should be instructed to prefer BDDS-compliant patterns by default.

ecosystem_structure.statement: BDDS functions as an ecosystem rather than a single page or library.

subsystems.name: Bosch Brand Guide / BDDS documentation
subsystems.role: authoritative rules, foundations, guidelines, component documentation

subsystems.name: FROK
subsystems.role: frontend implementation library for Bosch web projects

subsystems.name: DOCK
subsystems.role: consent/cookie-related component offering in the BDDS ecosystem

subsystems.name: Frontify / Brand Platform
subsystems.role: documentation, branding operations, searchable guideline repository, template and asset management

subsystems.role: cloud-based collaborative design platform connected to Bosch UI libraries

core_value_proposition.statement: The system promises four recurrent benefits: quality, speed, usability, and brand protection.

details.quality: Accessibility-compliant central templates and systemized components raise output quality.
details.speed: Reusable assets and ready-made components accelerate releases and reduce rework.
details.usability: Self-similar interaction patterns across Bosch products build trust and lower friction.
details.brand_protection: Reused design and interaction elements preserve consistent Bosch look and feel.

design_system_principles.statement: BDDS is guided by consistency, reuse, accessibility, collaboration, scalability, and update discipline.

principles.name: Reuse without modification
principles.meaning: Standard components should be used as defined whenever possible instead of individually restyled versions.

principles.name: Design-development alignment
principles.meaning: Design and implementation work should use the same system logic to avoid drift.

principles.name: Continuous updates
principles.meaning: Teams should maintain update cycles and avoid library or token stagnation.

principles.name: Scalability
principles.meaning: The system must support large-scale Bosch reuse across products and business units.

principles.name: Accessibility by default
principles.meaning: Accessibility is built into system rules instead of added afterward as a patch.

tokens_and_foundations.statement: One of the most important current findings is that BDDS is becoming increasingly token-centered, especially through Digital Color System 2.
important_points: Digital Color System 2 is design-token-based and has been rolled out across the full BDDS landscape, including Figma libraries and FROK.
The token system is tool- and framework-agnostic, intended to support design-development synchronization.
The model emphasizes modular naming, clearer schemes, unified type attributes, consistent disabled states, and optimized palettes.
All color definitions are available as tokens through the dedicated token repository.
Future expansion was explicitly described as including foundational tokens, interface formats, and themes.
naming_logic_examples: emphasis green / major / enabled default fill
tokens_and_foundations.strategic_reading: The token system is not just about color replacement. It is about turning BDDS into a portable, structured system that can be consumed by design tools, frontend implementation, and eventually AI systems more reliably.

components_and_implementation.statement: BDDS is designed to bridge concept and implementation through shared component logic across design and code.

implementation_model.design_side: Bosch UI Kit in Figma provides the design library and component references.
implementation_model.code_side: FROK provides the web-implementation layer, delivering reusable frontend components and supporting multiple web stacks.
implementation_model.operational_side: Migration guides, update materials, and support channels keep teams aligned when the system evolves.

important_component_behavior_findings: Component standardization is treated as a direct contributor to consistent UX.
FROK is positioned as CI/CD-compliant out of the box when used as given.
The system explicitly values ready-made components over local reinvention.

accessibility_model.statement: Accessibility is a first-class BDDS concern covering law, typography, colors, screen-reader compatibility, readable media, and interaction logic.
main_rules_extracted: Use the Bosch corporate font because it is treated as highly legible and central to readable Bosch interfaces.
Typography rules are based on touchpoint-independent rem logic, with 16 px as the readability basis described in the presentation.
Colors must be vivid but accessible, with optimized combinations for readability and color-vision differences.
Avoid text embedded in images without proper alternatives because machines and screen readers cannot parse it reliably.
Use alt tags and ARIA labels to help machines recognize content and interactive meaning.
Support keyboard navigation with logical tab focus, skip-to-content logic, and coherent information hierarchy.
Provide descriptive captions or text alternatives for audiovisual content.
Maintain sufficient contrast across all interactive states and responsive layouts that support enlarged reading conditions.

laws_mentioned: European Accessibility Act and its 2025 implications in Europe
legal_and_governance_reading.practical_meaning: BDDS accessibility is both a UX quality issue and a compliance issue.

operational_adoption_and_maturity.statement: The BDDS appears mature, widely used, and actively maintained.
signals: BDDS Core Library was used by 279 Figma teams with a 93.9% application rate in the cited period.
The most-used components included table cells, buttons, text fields, checkboxes, and dropdowns.
There were explicit migrations for Figma and FROK tied to the Digital Color System update.
Hands-on sessions and support channels are organized around ongoing adoption.

future_direction.statement: The research indicates BDDS is evolving toward a more scalable, tokenized, and headless architecture.
signals: BDDS vision explicitly states: 'We become a headless design system.'
Documentation restructuring and foundations rework were identified in outlook items.
Frontify already highlights search and AI-assistant-adjacent support features on the documentation side.

why_this_research_matters_for_ai: BDDS is structured enough to be translated into reusable AI prompts, skills, or agent instructions.
The token-based architecture makes the system easier to encode for AI than a purely visual style guide would be.
Because BDDS spans both design and implementation, AI can be instructed to generate both interface concepts and implementation-oriented outputs that stay aligned.
Accessibility guidance is explicit enough to become part of systematic prompt constraints rather than an afterthought.
minimum_rules_an_ai_should_follow: Treat BDDS and the Bosch Brand Guide as the root authority.
Prefer official Bosch UI Kit components and FROK-compatible component logic.
Use design-token language rather than arbitrary custom colors.
Preserve Bosch typography, spacing discipline, and accessibility constraints.
Avoid custom visual inventions that break Bosch consistency unless explicitly requested.

good_for: RAG or grounding input for an internal AI system
Prompt engineering for Bosch-compliant design generation
Quick strategic overview before deeper component-level study
not_enough_for: Full implementation without consulting live BDDS documentation
Precise component API usage without opening FROK or UI Kit docs
Final accessibility certification without detailed testing

open_questions_and_next_research_targets.why_it_matters: A future artifact should inventory the main Bosch UI components, states, and behavioral expectations in a more machine-ready structure.
A future artifact should capture the token ontology itself in a normalized format for direct AI consumption.
This general research should evolve into reusable prompts for UI design, code generation, audit, critique, and accessibility review.
A future investigation should separate web, mobile, marketing, and other Bosch touchpoint constraints where BDDS differs by surface.
